title: China has switched on 2,000 servers under the sea that nobody is allowed to touch
content: China has put a 24MW underwater data centre into commercial operation off Shanghai, sinking roughly 2,000 servers into pressure-resistant modules cooled by seawater and powered directly by an offshore wind farm. The Rs 2,000 crore Lingang facility claims a PUE under 1.15 and zero freshwater use. It builds on Microsoft's Project Natick, which sank 855 servers off Orkney in 2018, recorded one-eighth the failure rate of land servers, and was later abandoned.

title: What changed? Why the West is finally acting against Israel's 'settler terrorists'
content: European nations and the UK have adopted strong stances against Israeli settlement expansion.  These countries now consider settlement activities as ethnic cleansing and illegal under international law.  They have implemented import bans and sanctions on goods and individuals involved.  The United Nations has documented significant Palestinian displacement due to settler violence.  This marks a dramatic shift in the international community's response to the ongoing conflict.

title: Larry Ellison cancels $7.5bn Oracle stock sale over Europe's ‘timing’ concerns
content: Larry Ellison cancelled his Oracle stock sale plan shortly after its disclosure. No shares were sold under the arrangement which was set to expire later this year. This plan would have allowed the sale of fifty million Oracle shares. The cancellation highlights differences between US and European trading regulations for executives. Oracle's stock has experienced a decline while the company faces increased job cut costs.

title: Tasmania moved devils to Maria Island; 3,000-pair penguin colony disappeared
content: In 2012, 28 Tasmanian devils were introduced to Maria Island as an insurance population against facial tumour disease. The devils thrived, reaching up to 90, but experts say their presence came at a heavy cost to local wildlife. A survey later found Maria Island’s little penguin colonies had disappeared, wiping out an estimated 3,000 breeding pairs.

title: Australia opens $7.8m wastewater plant that treats 700 megalitres a year
content: This week, an innovative wastewater treatment facility was inaugurated in Dubbo, New South Wales, marking a significant upgrade in regional water management. Capable of processing large quantities of wastewater each year, the plant employs cutting-edge technology to effectively decompose challenging contaminants. The recycled water generated will have diverse applications, aiding local communities, especially in drought-affected areas, by transforming wastewater into a crucial resource.

title: Anthropic researcher says humanity's future decided on 'MacBooks of engineers'
content: Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon has quit the AI industry, saying OpenAI and Anthropic are racing to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives. His post, now past 155 million views, has pulled two more AI safety researchers out of Anthropic and Google and drawn a pacing plan from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, backed by Sam Altman and Elon Musk. Anthropic alignment lead Evan Hubinger puts the odds AI kills everyone above 10 per cent.

title: Where America’s richest shop for groceries and how much they spend
content: Affluent Americans are increasingly turning to Costco and Trader Joe's for their grocery shopping, visiting these stores more often each week. In contrast, Walmart Supercenters attract the majority of middle and lower-income families. This disparity in shopping habits highlights how different income levels can influence grocery spending and choices, illustrating the unique preferences and access available to various socioeconomic groups.

title: The Uranium rush: Inside India's scramble to fuel its nuclear ambitions
content: India is securing uranium fuel for its ambitious nuclear expansion program.  Uzbekistan, Australia, and Canada are key partners in this global fuel hunt.  New domestic laws allow private companies to build nuclear power plants.  This move creates significant demand for uranium fuel supplies.  India's long-term strategy also involves developing thorium resources.

title: How Travis Kelce turned his $3.13M rookie deal into a business empire

Collaborating with Jana Partners for a stake in Six Flags and joining an investment group for the Alpine Formula One team highlights his ambition, as he focuses on aligning his ventures with his personal passions while aligning them with opportunities to grow his brand.

title: How Trinity Rodman escaped Dennis Rodman’s shadow to build her own legacy
content: Trinity Rodman’s journey goes far beyond soccer. As a child, she lived with her mother and brother in a car and motels during a difficult period. Her mother, Michelle Moyer, became her biggest support and role model. Today, Trinity is an Olympic champion, NWSL champion and the league’s highest-paid player, after building her career on her own terms.

title: BSF rescues 10 Bangladeshi nationals, including children, from drowning in River Ganga
content: Border Security Force troops rescued ten Bangladeshi nationals from the Ganga River.  Their boat capsized in strong currents while crossing the Padma River.  Alert BSF personnel launched a swift rescue operation after noticing people struggling.  One infant was in critical condition but received immediate medical attention.  All rescued individuals were safely handed over to Bangladesh Border Guards.

title: From 55 to 65 homes a day: How factory robots are boosting housing production in the US
content: US homebuilders are adopting robotics to address worker shortages and boost housing supply.  Narrower automation applications are currently yielding the most significant improvements and efficiency gains.  Factory-based construction offers substantial potential for increasing housing production and reducing costs.  Skilled human workers will remain essential for complex and varied construction site tasks.  Robotics is expected to increase housing output over the next decade through targeted advancements.

title: Plugging gap: Why 67,000 EV charging points aren't enough for India’s electric dreams
content: By 2030, India is projected to require an additional 1.25 million electric vehicle (EV) charging stations. Currently, these public chargers are limited to just ten states, and the slower charging speeds provided by many of them may pose challenges during longer trips. While home charging is an option for individuals with private parking, operators struggle with low usage rates that deter investments in smaller urban areas.

title: How Gujarat’s villagers turned mangroves into a natural coastal shield

This significant recovery is attributed to community participation and large-scale plantation programmes. Mangroves provide vital coastal protection and support marine ecosystems and local livelihoods. The government now promotes this approach nationwide through the MISHTI programme. Gujarat's success demonstrates mangroves as effective natural infrastructure for coastal defense.

title: ‘Body lay on road for hours’: Blinkit delivery worker killed in bike accident

title: Canada explores ‘associate member’ status with EU amid US trade tensions

title: India’s semiconductor sector attracts $1.4 billion in funding across 281 companies

title: 'AAP will be extra cautious': Kejriwal on RS picks after Raghav Chadha exit
content:
Kejriwal on future Rajya Sabha picks after Raghav Chadha exit

NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party supremo Arvind Kejriwal on Sunday said he would be "extra cautious" while choosing the party's Rajya Sabha nominees in the future, referring to instances of its MPs leaving the party. Addressing a public gathering in poll-bound Goa, the former Delhi chief minister said, "AAP will be extra cautious while picking its Rajya Sabha nominees in future, following instances of its MPs leaving the party." Kejriwal's remarks come months after a major setback for AAP in the Rajya Sabha, with several of its MPs rebelling against the party leadership. Raghav Chadha, along with six other Rajya Sabha members, joined the BJP, significantly reducing AAP's strength and voice in Parliament. The Kejriwal-led party is preparing for next year's Goa assembly polls and has also announced a pre-poll alliance with the Goa Forward Party.

content: the backlog has grown by about 14,000 applications since august . the estimated processing time has risen from 25 months to more than 33 months . a surge follows the introduction of bill C-3 in December 2025, which removed first-generation limit on citizenship by descent .

title: Signal to West? Xi pitches for 'Greater Brics', rejects 'might makes right' logic
content: Xi said international rules must be written by all countries and rejected logic of "might makes right" he called for principles of sovereign equality, noninterference in internal affairs and peaceful settlement of disputes to be upheld, with international law applied to all without double standards .

title: Is UK heading for breakup? Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland push for independence
content: leaders of three devolved nations set to meet in Cardiff for unprecedented summit . they are expected to sign a joint declaration asserting their right to hold independence referendums . the gathering comes at a politically sensitive moment for Westminster .

title: 'Stop striking Russian refineries': Trump blames Ukraine for global diesel shortage
content: u.s. president says he has to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia . he says the attacks are contributing to a fuel shortage . the attacks have contributed to fuel rationing in parts of the country .

title: At 100, Barbara Haig still drives her Mustang, putting caution before age
content: a lifetime of seeing the world Travel has been one of the defining threads of Haig's life . she explored the united states and the world with a close friend she met through church . at an age when many people are content to slow down, she is still putting the top down .

title: Inside Martha Stewart’s 152-acre New York farm with 100 chickens
content: Martha Stewart bought a 152-acre farmhouse in Katonah, new york, in 2000 . it became a working farm, creative laboratory and carefully managed home for an ever-growing collection of animals . over the next 26 years, the property evolved into Bedford Farm, also known as Cantitoe Corners, with horses, gardens, historic and modern buildings .
